votes.reasoning: NotificationService.swift:141-150. A key is dropped only after 12 consecutive snapshots of its vendor fail to report it. Reappearing (line 141) or falling below the thresholds (line 128) resets the counter. I set the threshold back to 1 (the old immediate prune) and got two RED tests: NotificationThresholdTrackerTests.swift:68 (the notification fired again) and :57. Caveat, not a block: if crossings() is also called with empty windows on a failed fetch, 12 failures in a row would prune the key and allow one repeat notification. That is the intended behavior for a rolled label.

A one-line filter became a miss counter with a named constant, pruneAfterMissedSnapshots = 12, whose comment gives the reason and the real duration (about 1 h at 300 s). Nesting peaks at 3 (for / if / else) in a function under 40 lines. Removing entries while looping over highestNotified.keys is safe because Swift iterates a copy. missedSnapshots is cleared in both places where a key is re-armed or removed (NotificationService.swift:161, 287-295), so it cannot leak.

The change stays inside the tracker. Sources/AiTaskbarApp/NotificationService.swift:139-184 adds a private missedSnapshots map and pruneAfterMissedSnapshots = 12. It is in memory only: no persistence, no public API and no config key. The map is bounded because keys get removed when a window is seen again, when it falls below the minimum threshold, and when it is pruned.
